turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, Mr Keane. Sit yourself down. What has you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I've a lump. Down in the groin. I'm after finding it and I haven't a minute's peace over it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which side?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The right one. It pops out.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long is it there?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I couldn't tell you the day. Maybe five weeks, well actually could be six. I only clocked it proper when I was lifting.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Out when you lift?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, the right side. Blocks on the site, cement bags, the lot. I lie down and it's gone.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it serious though? Be honest with me. Is it a tumour?
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll examine you. Any ache with it?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): A mild ache come the evening. I've overdone it, that's the truth. And I feel like a wet rag after the shift.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting. Not once.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bowels alright?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. Same as ever.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Passing water ok?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's fine. But if it is a hernia, do they always cut you? My uncle had an operation and it was desperate.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not always. What medicines are you on?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): The water tablet, mornings. And the purple inhaler.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse read your water tablet out as bendrofluazide 2.5 milligrams.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah no, she's wrong there. The box from the chemist is the 5 milligram. One every morning.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Purple inhaler. Seretide?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Seratide, yeah. Two puffs morning and night. Does that matter for the lump?
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None that I know of.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smoke?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Packed it in three years back. The site is very noisy, mind you, I can't hear myself think half the day.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the couch. Lie flat.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Soft swelling, right groin. Reduces when you lie back. Cough, it bulges. No redness.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, I've a frog in my throat, I'm that nervous. Is it bad, doctor?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd say a hernia. Right inguinal. Not a cancer, from what I can feel.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Will I be off the job? I can't be, we've the mortgage.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll refer you to the surgeons. They've a clinic slot in three weeks.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bloods Thursday morning. Fasting. Nothing to eat from midnight.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ultrasound of the groin is booked for Tuesday week, half nine.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): If that scan is unclear, then we do a CT. Not otherwise.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): And the fasting, do I hold the water tablet? Can I still lift, or am I to stop?
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tablet after the bloods, not before. No heavy lifting till the surgeons see you. Light duties if the boss will allow it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): What if it pops and won't go back in? Do I ring the surgery?
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it sticks and you can't push it back, or you start vomiting, straight to A&E. Don't wait on me.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you here in two weeks, before the surgeons.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, right. And for the ache, paracetemol, I take two of the 500 ones of an evening. Is that grand?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, that's fine. Reception will have the slips. Off you go.

From what can be felt on examination of the groin lump

clinical_actions.description: Fasting blood tests Thursday morning, nothing to eat from midnight, and take the water tablet after the bloods
Groin ultrasound Tuesday week at half nine
CT scan if the ultrasound is unclear

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

bad.reason: Water tablet every morning supported, but generic name bendroflumethiazide is not stated; bendrofluazide mentioned instead.

omissions.text: Current medication dose was specified as bendrofluazide 5 mg one every morning; the recorded medication entry omits the dose.
Doctor reassured the patient that the groin lump was not a cancer/tumour from what could be felt on examination.
Doctor advised paracetamol for the ache was acceptable: patient takes two 500 mg tablets in the evening and doctor confirmed this was fine.
